transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samir Patel, Ava Chen (Redwood); Priya Singh, Tom Reynolds, Emily Park, Luis Martinez (MediSync)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed POC scope for data handling. Customer concerned about PII in prompts, prompt logging, retention windows, and whether Redwood hosted retains prompts. Redwood explained options: disable prompt retention, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), Dedicated/Private for full control, and redaction tooling. Agreed to share security docs and run benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you. quick intros - I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, Samir our SE is on the line, Ava in solutions.
[00:06] Priya: Hi, Priya Singh, Head of Data at MediSync. we run telehealth chat + triage, lots of PHI, so we need to get data handling nailed for POC.
[00:12] Tom: Tom Reynolds, CTO, I'll jump in on infra questions.
[00:15] Emily: Emily Park, security engineer. mainly here for compliance and retention stuff.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. high level: the POC goal is to validate accuracy and latency on typical triage flows, and to validate we can meet data handling rules. can you walk through your main constraints?
[00:30] Priya: Sure. main ones: (1) no storage of raw PHI in shared hosted logs, (2) audit trail/audit logs for all calls, (3) ability to redact or hash PII at ingestion, (4) retention windows we can configure - legal wants 30 days for prompt payloads and 6 years for audit metadata, and (5) SSO + RBAC so only certain folks can see logs.
[00:48] Emily: plus we need proof of encryption key management (customer KMS/HSM ideally) and SOC2 evidence.
[00:55] Samir: Understood. quick clarifying q: by "raw PHI in shared hosted logs" do you mean you don't want prompts or model contexts stored in Redwood's hosted analytics, or you want them redacted?
[01:05] Priya: Ideally we want them not stored in any multi-tenant hosted system unredacted. we could allow tokenized telemetry/metrics, but not raw prompts.
[01:14] Ava: OK that fits common patterns. we have three deployment approaches that matter here: hosted (fastest), dedicated (reserved capacity), private/VPC (on-prem style). Hosted by default retains short-term logs for debugging but we provide options to opt out of prompt retention for PII. Dedicated gives stronger isolation and can be configured to not persist prompts to long-term analytics. Private gives you full control and ability to bring your own keys.
[01:34] Tom: So for the POC what's the recommended path? we want speed but we need compliance.
[01:39] Jordan: For speed-to-PoC, many customers start hosted with prompt retention disabled + client-side redaction. we can disable prompt storage on your account and still run benchmarks. If you need KMS/HSM with BYOK, that's Dedicated or Private.
[01:50] Emily: What's the difference between disabling prompt storage and client-side redaction? 
[01:54] Samir: disabling prompt storage means we don't persist full prompt blobs in our analytics store. however transient logs for debugging may still exist for a short TTL unless you request stricter retention. client-side redaction removes or masks PII before it ever leaves your network - the safest but more engineering work.
[02:12] Priya: For POC we want Redwood to show they can run on non-prod data first. we'll provide synthetic records with PHI-like fields masked. but we need to be sure that Redwood won't index or keep those prompts.
[02:24] Jordan: Totally reasonable. we can sign up your POC account with prompt retention off and confirm via the audit logs. We'll also provide the data handling whitepaper and SOC2 docs.
[02:33] Luis: Quick perf q: for triage flows we estimate average ~250 tokens in, 500 tokens out, 30 concurrent users peak during test like 10-15 rps. what throughput are we expecting?
[02:44] Samir: That workload is light. we can run a benchmark at that shape. for hosted you should see single-digit 100s reqs per minute easily; Dedicated will give you predictable tail latencies. Our POC benchmark plan will include latency p95 and p99 targets.
[02:58] Tom: We need an SLO: p95 < 200ms for model generation? realistic?
[03:04] Samir: depends on model size and seq length. for medium-sized LLMs and the token counts you gave, p95 of 200-400ms is closer to reality on the most-optimized infra. we will include model variant comparisons; if you need <200ms consistently we may discuss Dedicated + quantized model variants.
[03:20] Emily: Back to data storage: how do you handle prompts that are part of error traces? are stacktraces or full payloads written to logs?
[03:28] Ava: Error traces may include payload snippets. we can set the logging level on your account to remove payloads entirely and only keep metadata (request id, timestamps, model version). we also support automatic PII redaction rules - regex-based and ML-based redaction - but customers prefer client-side redaction for PHI.
[03:45] Priya: Does Redwood provide redaction tools out of the box? or is this a partner integration?
[03:50] Samir: We provide a basic built-in redactor (configurable) and a redaction API you can run pre-send. It does false positives/negatives like any tool, so we strongly recommend combining with client-side pre-processing for PHI.
[04:03] Tom: On the encryption front: can we bring our own keys (BYOK) so that even if logs are retained they're encrypted under our KMS?
[04:10] Jordan: BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer server-side encryption and we can integrate with cloud KMS in some enterprise plans, but full BYOK where keys never leave your account is a Private/Dedicated feature.
[04:23] Emily: For audit requirements legal wants a full immutable audit trail of who accessed what and when for 6 years. Can Redwood keep that metadata while complying with our no-raw-prompt retention for 30 days?
[04:36] Ava: Yes. you can configure retention policies so that prompt bodies are purged after 30 days while metadata (request id, user id, timestamps, model version) is retained longer and exported to your SIEM. We support audit log exports to S3 or your log collection endpoint.
[04:50] Priya: Exporting to our SIEM is important. what's the format and frequency?
[04:54] Samir: We can stream logs in JSON with field-level filtering. Frequency can be near-real-time or batched; for POC we usually set up near-real-time to validate.
[05:03] Tom: OK. let's talk about prompt storage on Redwood's side: if we disable retention and do client-side redaction, how do we handle troubleshooting if something goes wrong during POC?
[05:12] Jordan: We can do a temporary opt-in window for detailed logs that you approve, or you can provide a repro with masked data. We also have a debug-mode that logs more detail to a secure location with limited access and TTL.
[05:24] Priya: We need to make sure debug-mode logs won't leak into any analytics buckets used by other customers.
[05:29] Ava: Debug logs for your account can be isolated and marked as non-multitenant; they won't be used for product analytics. we'll note that in the SoW for the POC.
[05:37] Emily: Can you show proof that prompt data is being purged? we need to validate in the POC that deletion actually happens.
[05:42] Samir: Yes, we can schedule a small retention test: upload synthetic prompts, then trigger purge and provide cryptographic proof via log of deletion events and S3 lifecycle events. we'll include that in the benchmark plan.
[05:52] Priya: Also concerned about embeddings. we use embeddings for search and they often include PHI. how does Redwood store embeddings and can they be disabled?
[06:00] Samir: Embeddings are stored if you call the embeddings API that persists them (e.g., in a vector DB). We don't automatically persist embeddings unless you use the managed embeddings store. For the POC, avoid managed storage or configure short retention. If you want embeddings persisted but encrypted under your KMS, that's available on Dedicated/Private.
[06:16] Luis: For success criteria, we propose: (1) Functional: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on synthetic triage set; (2) Performance: p95 latency <= 350ms for chosen model; (3) Security: no raw PHI retained beyond 30 days, audit logs retained 6 years and exportable.
[06:33] Jordan: Those are reasonable. we'll put those into the POC runbook.
[06:37] Tom: Timeline? we want to start running benchmarks within two weeks.
[06:41] Jordan: Sounds feasible. action plan: Jordan sends docs by 8/14, you provide data by 8/18, Redwood prepares benchmark plan by 8/20, run week of 8/25.
[06:53] Emily: Network-wise we may need a temporary IP allowlist for Redwood to reach our test env. can you provide the IP ranges and ports?
[06:59] Ava: yes, we'll include network diagrams and IP ranges in the security pack. for Private deployments there's a VPC setup doc too.
[07:08] Priya: A few more clarifying q's on prompt retention config: is it per-account or per-route? we might want different retention for triage vs analytics routes.
[07:18] Samir: Retention can be configured per-route. you can have different policies for /triage vs /analytics; that's a common setup.
[07:25] Priya: Great. is there an API to set retention programmatically?
[07:28] Ava: Yes, retention policies are part of the config API and Console. we'll share the API docs.
[07:34] Tom: On the compliance proof: we need exportable reports for SOC2 controls around logging access. do you provide role-level access logs?
[07:43] Samir: Yes, we log role-based access events. RBAC is integrated with SSO (SAML/OIDC) and we log who viewed what. we can export access reports for audits.
[07:53] Emily: One more: are there any scenarios where Redwood trains on our prompts or uses them for model improvement?
[07:59] Jordan: No. we do not train on customer prompts unless there is an explicit opt-in research program. For hosted accounts by default we do not use customer data to improve models; we'll include this statement in the contract.
[08:11] Priya: good. about prompt masking: do you provide libraries for redaction that our frontend/backend can call?
[08:17] Samir: We provide SDK helpers and example regex/NER models for redaction. those are in the data handling repo we'll share.
[08:25] Luis: Regarding benchmarks: will you simulate production concurrency patterns or will we run a synthetic steady-state?
[08:30] Samir: Both. the plan will include steady-state throughput and spike tests to measure tail latency and autoscaling behavior.
[08:37] Tom: For the POC contract, what are the limits? are there costs?
[08:41] Jordan: POC credits often cover the work; we'll include a limited trial credit and discuss Dedicated trial pricing if needed.
[08:48] Priya: Ok sounds good. let's reconfirm next steps and ownership.

Recap (auto): Jordan - send security pack by 8/14. Samir - benchmark plan and workload template by 8/20. Priya - synthetic dataset and PII mapping by 8/18. Emily - confirm retention policy checklist by 8/18. Schedule benchmark week of 8/25.

[09:10] Jordan: Any other questions?
[09:12] Emily: One last small ask: can you provide a sample deletion proof schema now so we can review with legal?
[09:18] Samir: yes we'll include the deletion proof format - it'll include event id, timestamp, object hash, and lifecycle event.
[09:25] Priya: great. thanks everyone.
[09:27] Jordan: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the pack.
